questions.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=k{x}^{2}+3x-15$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $4.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=3$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{3}{2(k)} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2k}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2k} & =4 \\ -3 & =8k \\ k & =-\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola $y=4{x}^{2}-16x+5.$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

We substitute $a=4$ and $b=-16$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-16)}{2(4)} \\  & =\frac{16}{8} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=2.$

questions.worked_solution:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-4$ and $b=-20$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-20)}{2(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{(-20)}{(-8)} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{5}{2}.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-\frac{5}{2}$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4{x}^{2}-20x-15 \\  & =-4{(-\frac{5}{2})}^{2}-20(-\frac{5}{2})-15 \\  & =-25+50-15 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-\frac{5}{2},10).$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-6$ and $b=36$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{36}{2(-6)} \\  & =-\frac{36}{(-12)} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=3$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-6{x}^{2}+36x-50 \\  & =-6(3)^{2}+36(3)-50 \\  & =-54+108-50 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(3,4).$

$$

Substituting $a=2$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(2)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{3}{2},$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{4} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ -2k & =12 \\ k & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
